narrative: OMX30 faces headwinds this morning despite remaining +2.1% above its 200-MA. European peers are uniformly negative (-0.68% to -0.72%), signaling coordinated risk-off sentiment. Technically, the index has triggered a bearish MACD crossover (hist=-1.699) and is trading in the lower half of Bollinger bands (%B=0.05), while the Stochastic K at 18.8 signals oversold conditions—classic mean reversion setup. The 50-MA at 3180 is now resistance; support lies at 3085 (lower Bollinger). The sharp US 10Y yield jump to 5.136% pressures tech/growth and real estate. With ADX at 15.9, trend conviction is weak, and the -0.385% weighted correlation bias is decidedly bearish.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to selling as Europe bleeds and US rates spike. Watch the 3150 level this morning—a break below opens 3085 (lower Bollinger). Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) face dual headwinds: elevated oil (+1.58%) and rising refinancing costs; however, USD/SEK strength (+0.04%) offers modest export support. Banks are caught between NIM upside (yields +0.74%) and credit cycle fears. Tech (Ericsson, Hexagon) under pressure from both NASDAQ weakness and multiple compression from higher rates. Stochastic oversold (K=18.8) suggests intraday bounce potential, but ADX weakness means any rally lacks conviction. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—misses could accelerate the risk-off. AI debt fears (per FT) keep volatility bid at VIX 18.65.
